rows.name: PYTHON_VERSION
rows.read_by: Workflow steps that run `uv sync`, and the step that runs `make deb` (`.github/workflows/cmake-single-platform.yml`, `.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`, `.github/workflows/cpp-coverage.yml` and 2 more files)
rows.values: Python version text with major, minor and patch numbers. All 5 workflows set `3.12.7`.
rows.default: Unset: no default exists. Each of the 5 workflows that read it defines it at workflow level.
rows.effect: The steps pass it to `uv sync --python` (`uv` is the Python package tool). `uv` then builds the Python environment of that step with this version. `publish-deb.yml` passes it to `make deb` as `TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION`.

It fails when two workflows give different values, when a value lacks the patch number, or when a value differs from the `TOKENIZER_PYTHON_VERSION` default in `GNUmakefile`.

rows.name: REGIONAL_NIX_CACHE
rows.values: URL of a Nix binary cache. The workflow sets `http://10.202.0.10:5000`. No script checks the text.
rows.default: Unset: no default exists. The workflow defines it at workflow level.
rows.effect: Four steps pass it to `bin/ci/nix-cache/acquire.py --cache`. The script copies one Nix store path from this cache with `nix copy --from`. The paths are outputs of the jobs `build-ingest`, `build-model-traces` and `generate-plugins`.
rows.notes: No script reads the name from the environment. `acquire.py` repeats a failed copy until 2700 seconds (45 minutes) have passed. It waits up to 15 seconds between two attempts. After the 2700 seconds it stops with `Could not acquire`.

rows.name: REQUESTED_RUNNER_CLASS
rows.read_by: Steps `Validate refresh invocation` and `Select runner matrix` of job `plan` (`.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`)
rows.values: `all`, `2x96core` or `2x72core`. Other text stops `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation` with `unknown runner class` and exit status 1.
rows.default: Unset: job `plan` always defines it. The value is `all` when the workflow input `runner_class` is empty, as on a scheduled run.

rows.name: ROLLOUT_ENABLED
rows.values: Copy of the repository variable `SLICE_REFRESH_ROLLOUT_ENABLED`. `bin/ci/bench-refresh-ci.sh validate-invocation` compares the text with `true`. Any other text counts as not enabled.
rows.default: Unset: job `plan` always defines it. The value is empty when the repository variable is not defined. Empty counts as not enabled.
rows.effect: Without the exact text `true`, `validate-invocation` stops a manual run that is not a dry run with `publishing refresh rollout is disabled`. It stops a scheduled run with `scheduled refresh rollout is disabled`.

rows.name: RUN_ATTEMPT
rows.read_by: Step `Run exact prebuilt benchmark` of job `benchmark` (`.github/workflows/gcp-nix.yml`)
rows.values: Whole number from the workflow expression `github.run_attempt`. The step tests whether it is greater than `1`.
rows.default: Unset: no default exists. The step always defines it.
rows.effect: A value above `1` adds `--force` to `bin/ci/tron-build/run_benchmark.sh`. The script then runs the benchmark again and does not reuse a stored result of an earlier run.

new_terms.definition: The workflow `.github/workflows/bench-refresh.yml`. It runs a full `bin/slice bench` measurement on each selected runner class. When the measurement changes the Slice cost data, it opens or updates a pull request for `config/test-benchmarks.json`.
A group of self-hosted CI servers of one type. The Slice cost-data refresh knows `2x96core` and `2x72core`.

new_terms.term: health check (of the Slice cost-data refresh)
new_terms.definition: The workflow `.github/workflows/bench-refresh-health.yml`. It fails when an expected runner class has no measured and published refresh in the last 14 days. A second job then opens, updates or closes the issue `Slice cost-data refresh is unhealthy`.

new_terms.term: dry run (of the Slice cost-data refresh)
new_terms.definition: A manual run of the refresh workflow with the input `dry_run` set to `true`. It measures and applies the result, and it opens no pull request.
The text `release-code@YYYY-MM-DD` that `bin/ci/bench_refresh_bitfile.py` builds from the release code and the release date that each FPGA card reports.
An empty file `<root>/<source hash>/nix-tests-<identity>.passed`. It records that the tests passed for one source hash, one test build and one Nix test environment.
The Nix store path with the tools that the CI test jobs run, for example `python3` and `uv`.
A top-level path of the form `/nix/store/<32 characters>-<name>`. A path inside such a directory is not a store root.
The Nix binary cache at the URL in `LAB_NIX_CACHE`. The test jobs and the benchmark jobs on FPGA servers copy their runtimes from it.

The JSON file `test-runtime.json` that job `tron-build` uploads as the artifact `tron-test-runtime`. It holds the commit id, the Nix store path of the test runtime and the Nix store path of the Nix test environment.
The Python package tool. `uv sync` builds a Python environment from a lock file.

notes: All 21 rows checked against the code at commit 7eddde7895. No row dropped, none missing. Every evidence quote of the input equals its source line. An existing claim was corrected in 10 rows. (1) PYTHON_VERSION: only the steps that read the name use the version. The Nix test and benchmark jobs take Python from their Nix environment. (2) ROLLOUT_ENABLED: on a scheduled run the job condition of plan tests the repository variable first. The manual case is the one that a person meets. (3) SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE_2X72CORE and (4) SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE_2X96CORE: the made-up example value is gone, the read_by file list holds only the file with the name, and the job stops before the measurement starts. (5) SLICE_REFRESH_2X72_ENABLED and (6) SLICE_REFRESH_ROLLOUT_ENABLED: the values cell no longer claims that every other text counts as not enabled, and bench-refresh-ci.sh left the read_by file list. (7) SLICE_REFRESH_MEASUREMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: an override and the stop time do not combine on a scheduled run. (8) SLICE_REFRESH_RUN_URL: an unset GitHub variable counts like an empty one. (9) SOURCE_HASH: prepare_handoff.py looks for the test pass marker and does not create it. (10) TEST_ENVIRONMENT_STORE_PATH: the empty value resolves to the working directory, publish_lab.py queues root files, and test_runtime.py does not resolve links. A fact was added in 9 more rows, with no change of an existing claim: REGIONAL_NIX_CACHE (wait and message), RUN_ATTEMPT (same-named shell variable in two scripts), RUN_TESTS (job names), SLICE_REFRESH_ALERT_ASSIGNEES (conditions of job reconcile), SLICE_REFRESH_STOP_UTC (stop message), SOURCE_SHA (use of the receipt field), and the doc/slice.md caller in SLICE_REFRESH_BITFILE, SLICE_REFRESH_RUNNER_CLASS and SLICE_REFRESH_SOURCE_SHA. REQUESTED_RUNNER_CLASS and SLICE_REFRESH_REVIEWERS are unchanged. Confirmed writer choices. A job-level env entry counts as workflow env (REQUESTED_RUNNER_CLASS, ROLLOUT_ENABLED, RUN_TESTS, SLICE_REFRESH_MEASUREMENT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS). SOURCE_HASH and SOURCE_SHA stay step env: a step of job tron-build writes them to the GITHUB_ENV file. The four names that only bin/ci/bench_refresh.py reads stay script. The two SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE names stay rows with source repository variable. Convention used here for the file lists. Every file path in read_by and who_sets contains the name. For the two SLICE_EXPECTED_BITFILE rows that leaves only bin/ci/bench_refresh_matrix.py: the reading workflow uses vars[matrix.expected_bitfile_var], and the cell says so in words. A test that sets a name is named in who_sets after the production setters. Not stated in the rows, on purpose: how a GitHub workflow expression compares the text True with 'true'. The checkout does not show it. New term added: runtime receipt. The definitions of Slice cost-data refresh, health check, bitfile identity and uv are reworded to match the code. Evidence quotes avoid source lines that hold a pipe character, as in the input.
